newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets price in rate cut.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets price in rate cut.

text.p: Australian markets go into waiting mode this week after last week's inflation and wages data reinforced the case for another monetary policy easing.
It seems the only question now is when it will happen after the Reserve Bank's silence at the end of last week.
A 50 basis point cut has already been priced into the local bond and forex markets.
But market participants will be keeping an eye on their screens at 9.30 a.m. every day just in case.

Domestic data due this week include the June balance of trade in goods and services on Tuesday and the key demand indicators of building approvals (June) on Wednesday and retail trade (June and June quarter) on Thursday.
Treasurer Peter Costello also speaks at an economic conference in Melbourne on Thursday.

Median forecasts of 27 economists polled by Reuters call for a 1.5 percent fall in building approvals after a 2.2 percent rise in May. Forecasts for retail sales come out at a rise of 0.4 percent for the month (up 2.9 percent in May) and 0.1 percent for the quarter (up 2.2 percent in March quarter).
(See Consensus report on AU/ECI for full forecasts).

The market will also be keeping an eye on key U.S. data, including the June quarter employment cost index on July 29, the first snapshot on Q2 GDP on July 31, and the big double of non-farm payrolls and the National Association of Purchasing Management survey on August 1.
AUSTRALIAN BONDS (Fri: 10-yr cash 6.51 pct, 3-yr 5.64 pct)
The Australian market, having already priced in a rate cut, is likely to start the week on a quiet note after a relatively quiet session in the U.S. markets ahead of this week's key data.

News of a 2.3 percent rise in durable goods orders for June -- the biggest rise since January -- had little impact and the 30-year Treasury bond closed with a yield of 6.46 percent, up from 6.44 percent at the close on Thursday.

Australian yields closed higher on Friday as the market took profits after a strong rally. Ten year bonds fell below 6.4 percent on Thursday, their lowest level since the mid 1980s, in response to inflation and wages data which appeared to clinch the argument that another rate cut was in the pipeline.

Economic data due this week are not expected to alter this view. "The bond market rally is close to exhaustion, particularly at the short end of the yield curve," Citibank economists said in weekly commentary.
"A 50 bp interest rate cut is well and truly priced in," the report said. "For the long end, there is also little upside, particularly on a spread basis."
"If the U.S. keeps rallying, however, domestic yields can track a little lower before the bearish phase sees 10-year yields move back to seven percent by the end of 1997."
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri: New York, US$0.7380, local $0.7405)

The local dollar staged a short-covering bounce on Friday in the absence of a rate cut but it eased again in New York trading. The dollar last week held within the US$0.7310/7440 range held for the second week and dealers said they doubted it would break out until the rate question was settled.
Dealers said resistance had already been felt at US$0.7420 and there was major chart resistance at US$0.7440 and US$0.7475.
However, there has been support beneath US$0.7330 and analysts expected these levels to hem in the currency ahead of any policy decision by the RBA.
SHARES (Fri: All Ordinaries 2,691.2, up 14.2)
Dealers said things were looking positive for shares this week, helped by the rate cut talk and Wall Street's firm tone.
"Quite clearly, there is a consensus that there will be a rate cut, and that won't change even if it doesn't happen (this) week," said a dealer at a Melbourne brokerage.
Corporate news remains relatively scarce with the reporting season yet to get into full swing.
"I think our market will probably be quite good next week", said Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan, noting attractive local valuations in comparison to other markets.
"The All Ordinaries is currently about 2690," Lourey said. "It has been fairly substantially over 2700 and I would see an improvement of maybe 25-30 points next week," he said.
Among scheduled events, pipe manufacturer G.E. Crane reports annual results on Monday and appliance maker Email Ltd holds its annual on Friday.
The market will also get its first chance to have its say on the proposed merger of Australis Media and Foxtel announced after the close on Friday.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
